set -o pipefail && mkdir -p output &&
python '$__tool_directory__/idr_download_by_ids.py'
#if $omero_instance_type.omero_instance == 'priv' omero #set $sel = $omero_instance_type.image_ids #if $sel.selection == 'dataset' --dataset $sel.id_dataset_omero #else #for $image_id in str($sel.id_spec).split() '$image_id' #end for #end if
#set $reg = $omero_instance_type.image_region --mode $reg.mode #if $reg.mode == 'plane' -z $reg.z_section #if str($reg.channel).strip() -c '$reg.channel' #end if -t $reg.frame #elif $reg.mode == 'stack' #if str($reg.tile).strip() --tile ${str($reg.tile).replace(',', ' ')} #end if -c '$reg.channel' -t $reg.frame #end if
#if $omero_instance_type.original --original #end if #if $omero_instance_type.skip_failed --skip-failed #end if @HOST_PORT@
#elif $omero_instance_type.omero_instance == 'idr' #set $q = $omero_instance_type.query #if $q.type == 'image' image #for $image_id in str($q.id_spec).split() '$image_id' #end for #if $q.skip_failed --skip-failed #end if #elif $q.type == 'annotation' annotation '$q.value' '$q.object_type' #else bulk '$q.id_file' #end if #end if
-o output 2>&1 | tee '$log'
#if $zip && tar -czf '$output_tar' output #end if

tool.help:
@SECURITY_DISCLAIMER@ **What it does**
This tool allows users to fetch images and annotations (tables and key-value pairs) directly from the [Image Data Resource (IDR)](https://idr.openmicroscopy.org), and images from a private OMERO server.
For Zarr images, the tool provides links to their S3/HTTPS storage locations, together with a link for NGFF validation. Other image file formats are downloaded as original files, up to a maximum of 20 files per image; if an image has more than 20 files, only links are provided.
Images stored in OMERO can be fetched as single-plane (YX), stack (ZYX), hypercube TIFF (ZCTYX), or as the original files.
**Downloading from IDR**
Choose what to fetch:
- **Images**: Enter a single image ID, or a space-separated list of image IDs (for example, `54321 54322 54323`). - **Key-Value pairs annotation**: Choose the object type (Image, Project, Screen or Well) and enter its ID. All key-value pairs (map annotations) attached to that object are saved as a TSV file with the columns namespace, key and value. - **Tables**: Enter a Screen ID. The `bulk_annotations` table (OMERO.table) attached to that screen is saved as a TSV file.
**Downloading from a private OMERO server**
Enter the server hostname and port. Your OMERO username and password, or an existing session key, are taken from the OMERO credentials stored in your Galaxy user preferences. The OMERO credentials of older versions of this tool (stored as user preference fields) are no longer used, so please enter them again in the credentials section.
Images can be selected by image ID (one or more, separated by spaces) or by OMERO dataset ID. If a dataset ID is selected, all images in that dataset are downloaded.
Then choose what to download:
- **Export - Plane**: Downloads a single plane defined by the channel index, z-plane, and time point (all indices start at 0). The output is a 2D image (YX). - **Export - Stack**: Downloads all z-planes for a single channel and time point as a TIFF file. The output is a 3D image (ZYX). The download can be limited to a tile specified as `x,y,width,height` in pixels, where `x,y` is the upper-left corner. - **Export - Hypercube**: Downloads all dimensions as a TIFF file. The output is a 5D image (ZCTYX). - **Original**: Downloads the files exactly as originally uploaded to OMERO, rather than exporting them. Files shared by several images (one fileset) are downloaded only once.
If a session key is used, the session is left open after the job; a session opened with username and password is closed.
**Failed downloads**
With "Continue if some IDs cannot be downloaded?" set to **Yes**, missing or failing images are listed in the log and everything else is returned. With **No**, the job fails if any image could not be downloaded (the other images are still attempted, but no output is returned).
**Output**
A **log** file lists the downloaded images and any warnings or errors.
The downloaded images are returned either as a **tarball** containing all downloaded images (default; recommended for many images) or as a **collection** of individual images when “Download images in a tarball?” is set to **No**.
The collection option is recommended only for a small number of images.
